entry.title: GRPO Experiments
entry.content:
In GRPO, value network (critic) is removed to save memory. To estimate advantages, we sample mulitple responses and do normalization within the group to estimate advantages. Specifically

\( egin{align} \mathbb{A}(i) &= rac{r_{i} - \mathbb{mean}(r_{1}, r_{2}, \dots, r_{G})}{\mathbb{std}(r_{1}, r_{2}, \dots, r_{G})} \ \mathbb{J}( heta) &= rac{1}{G}\sum_{i=1}^{G} rac{1}{T_{i}}\sum_{t=0}^{T_{i}-1}\left(\min\left( rac{\pi_{ heta}(a_{i,t}|s_{i,t})}{\pi_{ heta}^{old}(a_{i,t}|s_{i,t})}\mathbb{A}_{i,t},clip\left( rac{\pi_{ heta}(a_{i,t}|s_{i,t})}{\pi_{ heta}^{old}(a_{i,t}|s_{i,t})}, 1-\epsilon, 1+\epsilon ight)\mathbb{A}_{i,t} ight) ight) \end{align}\) where $a_{i,t}$ is the token generated at time $t$ in response $i$. All tokens in the response have the same advantage.

Experiments

Github project

Due to limit GPU memory (24GB Nvidia RTX 3090), we use QLora for GRPO. More specifically, we

  1. load base model in 4bits and freeze it
  2. train a Lora adapter (rank=64, dtype=bf16)
  3. reward functions are the same as in Unsloth colab
    • format reward:
      • exact: exact format matching, <reasoning> ...< easoning> <answer> ...<\answer>
      • approximate: allow spaces
      • html tag: reward if there are html tags (<reasoning>, < easoning>, <answer>, <\answer>) in response
    • correctness reward
      • strict: match the answer
      • fuzzy: answer is integer
  4. use train split from GSM8K dataset as prompts
  5. evaluate on test split from GSM8K

Prompt

  • Base prompt
    • in system prompt we add detailed instruction (probably too much as we already tell the model the answer should be an integer). We do this because sometimes we notice format issue in the base model ```Respond in the following format: Put your reasoning here. Put your answer here. The answer should be an integer.

      ```

    • in user prompt, we explicitly state “let’s think step by step” {question} Let's think step by step.. We do this because otherwise the baseline metric is much lower.
  • GRPO prompt
    • in system prompt, we use simpler instruction ```Respond in the following format: ... ...

      ```

    • in user prompt, we just add the question {question} without think step by step.

Qwen 2.5 3B Instruct

Model PASS@1
Base 69.7%
GRPO 81.1%

Training

We notice that

  • the reward goes up after ~250 steps. This is also mentioned in Unsloth colab that at least 250 steps are needed to see improvement
  • after 250 steps, the reward doesn’ts change much
  • the length flucutate a bit without increasing significantly. This is probably due to the base model is already post trained

entry.title: PPO in post training
entry.content:
This is a blog to record my learning of PPO. I have been working on RLHF for a while. But I always feel I cannot connect all dots together to have a good overall understanding. This blog is to record my understanding and will be used for my own reference. I’m lazy so I didn’t include the references I read.

High Level Understanding

On the high level, the actor generates responses and reward model gives rewards. For responses with high rewards, the actor increases the probabiliy. For responses with low rewards, the actor decreases the probabiliy.

So, the objective is roughly

\( egin{align} \max_{ heta}\sum_{ au\sim\pi_{ heta}}[R({ au})\mathbb{P}( au; heta)] \end{align}\) Where $ au$ is a samppled trajectory.

Intuitively, in order to maximize this objective

  • If the reward $R({ au})$ is positive, we should increase $\mathbb{P}( au; heta)$
  • If the reward $R({ au})$ is negative, we should decrease $\mathbb{P}( au; heta)$

Note the differences between SFT and RL are

  • SFT:
    1. Immitation: model tries to immitate the given (positive) targets
    2. offline: targets $\mathbb{D}$ are generated offline by human or other models
    3. SFT’s objective is to $\max_{ heta}\sum_{ au\sim\mathbb{D}}\mathbb{P}( au; heta)$
  • RL:
    1. online: actor generates rollouts and reward model gives rewards
    2. rewards can be negative and positive
    3. actor tries to increase the probability of rollouts with high rewards while decrease the probability of rollouts with low rewards

Policy Gradient

Starting with policy gradient, the goal is to maximize the expected return

\[ egin{align} J(\pi_{ heta}) = \mathbb{E}_{ au\sim\pi_{ heta}}[R( au)] \end{align}\]

Where we sample trajectory $ au$ from actor $\pi_{ heta}$.

Now, we can take the gradient of $J$

\( egin{align} abla_{ heta} J(\pi_{ heta}) &= abla_{ heta}\mathbb{E}_{ au\sim\pi_{ heta}}[R( au)] \ &= abla_{ heta}\sum_{ au}R( au)P( au; heta) \ &= \sum_{ au}R( au) abla_{ heta}P( au; heta) \ &= \sum_{ au}R( au) abla_{ heta}\log P( au; heta)P( au; heta) \ &= \mathbb{E}_{ au\sim \pi_{ heta}}[R( au) abla_{ heta}\log P( au; heta)] \ &= \mathbb{E}_{ au\sim \pi_{ heta}}[R( au)\sum_{t=0}^{\infty} abla_{ heta}\log \pi_{ heta}(a_{t}|s_{t})] \ &= \sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\mathbb{E}_{a_{t}\sim \pi(\cdot|s_{t})}[R_{t} abla_{ heta}\log \pi_{ heta}(a_{t}|s_{t})] \ &= \mathbb{E}_{t}[R_{t} abla_{ heta}\log \pi_{ heta}(a_{t}|s_{t})] \end{align}\) where $R_{t}$ is the discounted reward starting from timestamp $t$.

The counter intuitive part here is that we first derive the gradient. In order to use backprop to optimize, we need to fine a surrogate loss function which when taking gradient w.r.t. $ heta$, we get the exact same gradient.

The loss function is defined as

\[ egin{align} \mathbb{L}_{pg}( heta) &= -\mathbb{E}_{t}[R_{t}\log \pi_{ heta}(a_{t}|s_{t})] \end{align}\]

It has high variance due to

  1. we only sample a few trajectories when computing the gradient
  2. we attribute response reward equally back to each token

REINFORCE

To reduce the variance, we can substract a baseline from the reward.

\( egin{align} abla_{ heta} J(\pi_{ heta}) &= \mathbb{E}_{t}[(R_{t}-b_{t}) abla_{ heta}\log \pi_{ heta}(a_{t}|s_{t})] \end{align}\) Where $b(t)$ is usually the average reward across the batch. This is unbiased because $b(t)$ is indenpendent of $a_{t}$.

\( egin{align} \mathbb{E}_{t}[ abla_{ heta}\log \pi_{ heta}(a_{t}|s_{t})] &= \sum_{a_{t}\sim\pi_{ heta}({\cdot|s_{t}})}\left[ rac{ abla_{ heta}\pi_{ heta}(a_{t}|s_{t})}{\pi_{ heta}(a_{t}|s_{t})}\pi_{ heta}(a_{t}|s_{t}) ight] \ &= abla_{ heta}\mathbb{E}_{t}[ \sum_{a_{t}\sim\pi_{ heta}({\cdot|s_{t}})}\pi_{ heta}(a_{t}|s_{t})]= abla_{ heta}1=0 \end{align}\)

PPO

Policy Loss

We have following equation \( egin{align} \mathbb{E}_{ au\sim\pi}[R( au)] = \mathbb{E}_{s_{0}\sim ho_{s}}[V^{\pi}(s_{0})] \end{align}\)

where \(\mathbb{E}_{ au\sim\pi}[R( au)]\) is the expected total reward from trajectories and \(\mathbb{E}_{s_{0}\sim ho_{s}}[V^{\pi}(s_{0})]\) is the expected value from starting state.

Given an old policy $\pi_{ heta_{old}}$, we have following reward

\( egin{align} \mathbb{J}( heta_{old}) &= \mathbb{E}_{s_{0}\sim ho_{s}}[V^{\pi_{ heta_{old}}}(s_{0})] \ &= \mathbb{E}_{s_{0}\sim ho_{s}}[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}V^{\pi_{ heta_{old}}}(s_{t}) - \sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}V^{\pi_{ heta_{old}}}(s_{t})] \ &= \mathbb{E}_{\pi_{ heta}}[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}V^{\pi_{ heta_{old}}}(s_{t}) - \sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}V^{\pi_{ heta_{old}}}(s_{t})] \end{align}\) Because $s_{0}$ is independent of $\pi_{ heta}$.

Now, suppose we come up a new policy $\pi_{ heta}$. The reward is \( egin{align} \mathbb{J}( heta) &= \mathbb{E}_{\pi_{ heta}}[V^{\pi_{ heta}}(s_{0})] \ &= \mathbb{E}_{\pi_{ heta}}[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}r(a_{t}, s_{t})] \end{align}\)

The reward difference between the new and old policies is

\[ egin{align} \mathbb{J}( heta)-\mathbb{J}( heta_{old}) &= \mathbb{E}_{s_{0}\sim ho_{s}}[V^{\pi_{ heta}}(s_{0})] - \mathbb{E}_{s_{0}\sim ho_{s}}[V^{\pi_{ heta_{old}}}(s_{0})]\ &= \mathbb{E}_{\pi_{ heta}}[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}r(a_{t}, s_{t})]-\mathbb{E}_{\pi_{ heta}}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}V^{\pi_{ heta_{old}}}(s_{t}) - \sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}V^{\pi_{ heta_{old}}}(s_{t}) ight] \ &= \mathbb{E}_{\pi_{ heta}}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}r(a_{t}, s_{t})-\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}V^{\pi_{ heta_{old}}}(s_{t}) + \sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}V^{\pi_{ heta_{old}}}(s_{t}) ight] \ &= \mathbb{E}_{\pi_{ heta}}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}(r(a_{t}, s_{t}) - V^{\pi_{ heta_{old}}}(s_{t}) + \gamma V^{\pi_{ heta_{old}}}(s_{t+1})) ight] \ &= \sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\mathbb{E}_{a_{t}\sim\pi_{ heta}(\cdot|s_{t})}\left[\gamma^{t}(r(a_{t}, s_{t}) - V^{\pi_{ heta_{old}}}(s_{t}) + \gamma V^{\pi_{ heta_{old}}}(s_{t+1})) ight] \ &= \mathbb{E}_{t}\left[\gamma^{t}(r(a_{t}, s_{t}) - V^{\pi_{ heta_{old}}}(s_{t}) + \gamma V^{\pi_{ heta_{old}}}(s_{t+1})) ight] \ &= \mathbb{E}_{t}\left[\gamma^{t}A(a_{t}, s_{t}) ight] \end{align}\]

We would like to find a new policy $\pi_{ heta}$ such that \(\mathbb{E}_{t}\left[\gamma^{t}A(a_{t}, s_{t}) ight]>0\). In practice, instead of maximizing the global objective. PPO maximizes the local objective, a mini batch. So $\gamma^{t}$ is applied when computing advantages.

Now, we have \( egin{align} \max_{ heta}\mathbb{E}_{t}\left[A(a_{t}, s_{t}) ight] \end{align}\)

Since we take expectation w.r.t. $\pi_{ heta}$ and we sample trajectories from $\pi_{ heta_{old}}$. Using importance sampling, we get

\( egin{align} \max_{ heta}\mathbb{E}_{t}\left[r_{t}( heta)A(a_{t}, s_{t}) ight] \end{align}\) Where $r_{t}( heta)= rac{\pi_{ heta}(a_{t}/s_{t})}{\pi_{ heta_{old}(a_{t}/s_{t})}}$.

To avoid large update, PPO also clips the ratio $r_{t}( heta)$. The final PPO policy loss is \( egin{align} \mathbb{L}_{ppo-policy}( heta)=-\mathbb{E}_{t}\left[\min(r_{t}( heta)A(a_{t}, s_{t}), clip(r_{t}( heta), 1-\epsilon, 1+\epsilon)A(a_{t}, s_{t})) ight] \end{align}\)

Another Hand-waving way to derive PPO policy is to use Policy Gradient loss funciton. Recall, the loss function is

\[\mathbb{L}_{pg}( heta) = -\mathbb{E}_{t}[R_{t}\log \pi_{ heta}(a_{t}|s_{t})]\]

In genereal, we replace $R_{t}$ by $A_{t}$ to reduce variance. We also have

\( egin{align} abla_{ heta}\mathbb{L}_{pg}( heta) &= -\mathbb{E}_{t}[R_{t} abla_{ heta}\log \pi_{ heta}(a_{t}|s_{t})] \ &= -\mathbb{E}_{t}[R_{t} rac{ abla_{ heta}\pi_{ heta}(a_{t}|s_{t})}{\pi_{ heta}(a_{t}|s_{t})}] \end{align}\) So we replace $\log \pi_{ heta}(a_{t}|s_{t})$ by $ rac{\pi_{ heta}(a_{t}|s_{t})}{\pi_{ heta_{old}}(a_{t}|s_{t})}$.

GAE

\( egin{align} A(t) &= \delta_{t} + \gamma \lambda A(t+1) \ \delta_{t} &= r(t) + \gamma V(s_{t+1}) - V(s_{t}) \end{align}\)

  • If $\lambda=0$, we have $A(t)=\delta(t)$ which is time difference. This is high bias low variance.
  • If $\lambda=1$, we have $A(t)=\delta(t) + \gamma A(t+1)$ which is monte carlo simulation using all trajectory. This is high variance low bias.

GAE sits in between to balance the bias and variance.

In implementation, each token has KL loss as reward. The last token recieves the reward. Then we compute advantages backwards.

KL Loss

KL loss is introduced in the advantage. By definition, KL divergence is computed over the full vocab

\[KL[\pi_{ heta}(\cdot|s_{t})||\pi_{ref}(\cdot|s_{t})] = \sum_{a_{t}\in V}\pi_{ heta}(a_{t}|s_{t})\log rac{\pi_{ heta}(a_{t}|s_{t})}{\pi_{ref}(a_{t}|s_{t})}\]

In practice, we only compute KL on sampled tokens as an approximation

\[KL_{approx} = \log rac{\pi_{ heta}(a_{t}|s_{t})}{\pi_{ref}(a_{t}|s_{t})}\]
